The *Pādapīṭhiyattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text located in the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It preserves the narrative verses attributed to the elder (thera) Pādapīṭhiya, recounting his past meritorious deeds and spiritual attainments [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages, but identifies no curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral].

The most significant alignment occurs with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), where segments 8.2–9.1 correspond closely with commentary sections 4234–4236 [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares substantial stock sequences (notably around segments 8.2–13.1) with numerous fellow poems in the Therāpadāna, such as *Pādaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 507), *Ghosasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 520), *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 459), and *Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 495) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus reports machine alignments with the Sanskrit *Divyāvadāna* (e.g., segment 7.3–7.4 aligning with section 4387), reflecting shared conventional phrases rather than an established direct parallel [DharmaNexus].
